patients.summary: Retired math teacher with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and BPH who joins in 2021. Recurrent urinary retention after a hernia repair, a knee replacement and on its own, orthostatic hypotension on tamsulosin, hyperkalemia on sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim with lisinopril, and a UTI-related delirium admission in 2025. Outside records reach the practice unevenly.

documents.title: New Patient Inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mr. Bennett phoned. Retired, lives in Belchertown, wants to transfer primary care here from the office he has used for years; a neighbor is a member. Explained membership, he signed up over the phone. New patient visit booked for next Tuesday morning, 60 min. Asked him to bring all his pill bottles and any recent lab printouts. Records release form emailed to edward.bennett@example.test.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT
69 y/o retired high school math teacher transferring care. Married, lives with his wife in Belchertown.

DIABETES: type 2 for many years, metformin 1000 twice a day, tolerates it. Checks sugars a few mornings a week, usually 120s-140s. No lows. No numbness or foot sores. Eye exam yearly with his optometrist.
HYPERTENSION: lisinopril 10 daily, home cuff runs low 130s.
STATIN: atorvastatin 20, started by his old PCP for the diabetes. No muscle aches.
RIGHT KNEE: arthritis, sees an outside orthopedic group, walks most days, says the knee is 'manageable for now.'
GU: no urinary complaints today.

PMH: as above. PSH: none.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: none known to medications.
FH: father type 2 diabetes, died of prostate cancer at 75. Mother hypertension. Older brother has an enlarged prostate.
SH: never smoker. A beer or a glass of wine once or twice a week. Retired from teaching math.

ROS: negative except knee as above.
EXAM: well appearing. BP and HR per flowsheet. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abd soft, nontender. Feet: skin intact, DP pulses 2+, monofilament normal both feet. Right knee crepitus, no effusion.

A/P
1. T2DM: continue metformin. A1c, CMP, urine albumin today.
2. HTN: at goal, continue lisinopril.
3. Statin: continue atorvastatin 20, lipids today.
4. R knee OA: per ortho.
5. Health maintenance: will get old records (colonoscopy, vaccines). Hep C screen today. PHQ-2 negative.
Follow up after the records come in; AWV in the fall.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Edward, your bloodwork is back. A1c is right where we want it for you, kidney function and potassium are normal, cholesterol is in a good range on the atorvastatin, and the urine protein test is normal. Hepatitis C screen negative. No changes. I'll see you in the fall for your wellness visit.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you, good to hear. My old office never explained the numbers this clearly. Ed

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL WELLNESS VISIT - INITIAL
Health risk assessment reviewed with him. Independent in daily activities, still drives, does the grocery shopping. Walks 2 miles most mornings unless the knee complains. No falls this year. Hearing ok. Vision followed by optometry, no retinopathy in August.
Cognition: brief screen normal, sharp as ever (he corrected my arithmetic on the copay).
Mood: PHQ-2 0.
Advance directive: wife is his health care proxy, will bring a copy.
Screening: colonoscopy 2017 normal per old records. Hep C done in June. Shingrix and Tdap up to date.
Vaccines today: high-dose flu L deltoid, PCV20 R deltoid. Tolerated.
Plan: diabetes visit in December.

documents.title: Same-Day Visit: Dysuria
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted this morning, seen same day.
S: 2 days of burning when he urinates and going more often. No fever or chills, no flank pain, no blood he has noticed. First time for this. No discharge.
O: afebrile, vitals per flowsheet. Abdomen soft, mild suprapubic discomfort to palpation, no CVA tenderness.
UA dip: LE 2+, nitrite positive.
A/P: cystitis in a man, so treating as a complicated UTI. Culture sent. Cephalexin 500 four times daily x7 days. Fluids. Call if fever, back pain, or not improving in 48 h. We'll call with the culture.

documents.title: Urine Culture Result
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt with culture: E. coli, sensitive to the cephalexin he is on. He says the burning is already better. Reminded to finish all 7 days. PCP aware.

documents.title: Finished antibiotic
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Finished the antibiotic last week and everything is back to normal. Thanks for fitting me in that day.

documents.title: RE: Finished antibiotic
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad to hear it. No need to recheck unless symptoms come back.

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
DM/HTN f/u.
Doing fine. Fasting sugars 130s. No hypoglycemia. Taking all meds.
Mentions he has been getting up 2 or 3 times a night to urinate since around October, and goes more often in the day. No burning since the UTI. Thinks it might be the extra decaf in the evening.
Exam: BP/HR per flowsheet. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Feet intact.
A/P
- T2DM: A1c drawn today, continue metformin.
- HTN: controlled, lisinopril.
- Nocturia/frequency: cut evening fluids, watch for a couple of months; if it continues, examine and consider treatment.
RTC 2 months.

documents.title: A1c and BMP

documents.body: A1c stable, BMP normal. Released to portal with a short note.

documents.author: MA

documents.title: Office Visit: Urinary Symptoms
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back about the urinary symptoms. Cutting fluids after dinner didn't help much.
Now about 4 months of going every couple of hours, up 2-3x a night, slow to get started, and a weaker stream than he used to have. No pain, no blood, no fever. Brother has the same thing, and father died of prostate cancer, so he's anxious about that.
Exam: GU deferred to urology per his preference. Abdomen soft, no bladder palpable.
UA dip clean today.
A/P: LUTS, most likely prostate enlargement. Start tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; counseled about lightheadedness when standing, especially the first few doses, and to take it after the same meal. Referral to urology for full evaluation including PSA given family history. RTC after urology.

conditions.label: Benign prostatic hyperplasia with lower urinary tract symptoms

documents.title: Urology Consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
UROLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 04/20/2022
Referred by primary care for voiding symptoms.

Mr. Bennett is a 70-year-old man with roughly half a year of daytime frequency, getting up at night to void, a slow start and a weakened stream. Urination is painless. One treated UTI in November. Started tamsulosin 0.4 mg in February through his PCP with modest effect so far.
PMH: type 2 diabetes, hypertension (well controlled), right knee osteoarthritis.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father died of prostate cancer at age 75. Brother with BPH.
Social: never smoker, social alcohol.

Exam: BP 135/85, HR 78, BMI 29. Abdomen soft, bladder not palpable. Normal phallus and testes. DRE: prostate enlarged symmetrically, firm texture, no nodules, nontender.
UA: no evidence of infection, no hematuria.
Labs (drawn today): creatinine 1.0, fasting glucose 140, PSA 2.8 ng/mL.

Impression: benign prostatic hyperplasia with lower urinary tract symptoms. PSA within the age-adjusted range and exam benign; reassuring despite his father's history.
Plan: continue tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. Reviewed behavioral measures. Return in 6 months with post-void residual.

Thank you for this referral.
Urology

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Interval: saw urology in April, BPH with a benign exam and a normal-range PSA, letter reviewed. On tamsulosin, nights a little better, still up twice.
DM: home sugars 120-150. Metformin, no GI issues.
HTN: home readings fine.
No dizziness on standing.
Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Heart regular, lungs clear. Monofilament intact both feet, no calluses.
Plan: A1c, BMP, lipids, urine albumin. Continue all meds. Urology again in the fall. AWV September.

documents.title: Lab Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yearly diabetes labs reviewed: A1c in his usual range, kidney function and potassium normal, LDL at goal on atorvastatin 20, urine albumin normal. Portal note sent. No changes.

documents.title: Same-Day Visit: UTI Symptoms
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Second UTI-type episode in 8 months. Burning and urgency since Sunday, more frequent than his usual baseline. No fever, no flank pain.
Vitals per flowsheet, afebrile. No CVA tenderness, mild suprapubic tenderness.
UA positive for LE and nitrite, trace blood on dip.
A/P: recurrent cystitis in a man with BPH. Culture sent. Cephalexin 500 QID x7d again (last culture was sensitive). Will let urology know at the fall visit; incomplete emptying may be contributing. Trace blood: recheck UA after treatment.

documents.title: Culture Result Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Culture grew E. coli again, sensitive to cephalexin. Spoke with pt, symptoms improving on day 3. Continue course. UA recheck to be done when he comes in for the AWV in September.

documents.title: All better
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Done with the capsules, no burning anymore. Will do the urine test in September like the nurse said.

documents.author: PCP

AWV (subsequent).
Functional status unchanged: drives, walks most days, does the yard. No falls. Knee about the same, ortho following.
Cognition screen normal. PHQ-2 0.
UA recheck after July UTI: no blood, no leukocytes.
GU: urology follow-up booked for October 10.
Advance directive copy now scanned.
Flu vaccine (high dose) given today. Bivalent COVID booster at a nurse visit later in October.
Next diabetes visit December.

documents.title: Urology Follow-up
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
UROLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Visit date: 10/10/2022

Returns 6 months after his first evaluation for BPH. Over the past half year he describes frequency, urgency and nocturia and feels he does not empty completely. Two urinary infections in the last 12 months, both treated with antibiotics by primary care.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: abdomen soft and nontender. DRE: symmetrically enlarged, firm, nontender gland, no nodules.
Urinalysis: no evidence of active infection.
Labs: creatinine 1.2, BUN 18.
Bladder ultrasound post-void residual: 120 mL.

Assessment: BPH with LUTS and an incomplete-emptying component; recurrent UTIs.
Plan: continue tamsulosin. Double voiding. Follow up as needed.

Urology
